summary: --limit narrows ad hoc targets to one host, several, a group, or a negated set (single-quoted to avoid bash expansion).
questions: How do I run an ad hoc command on just one host?
How do I exclude a host with --limit?
Why do I need single quotes for --limit with !?

answer_card.title: Use --limit with ad hoc commands
answer_card.answer_md:
```bash
ansible all -m <module> -a "<opts>" --limit "host1"
ansible all -m <module> -a "<opts>" --limit "host1,host2"
ansible all -m <module> -a "<opts>" --limit 'all:!host1'   # single quotes required
ansible all -m <module> -a "<opts>" --limit 'group1'
```
